description: Technical design document with implementation details
instruction:
Create the design document that explains HOW to implement the change.

When to include design.md (create only if any apply):
- Cross-cutting change (multiple services/modules) or new architectural pattern
- New external dependency or significant data model changes
- Security, performance, or migration complexity
- Ambiguity that benefits from technical decisions before coding

Sections:
- **Context**: Only the current state and constraints needed to explain the approach. Reference the proposal for motivation instead of restating it (e.g., "See proposal.md - Why").
- **Goals / Non-Goals**: What this design achieves and explicitly excludes. Don't restate the proposal's scope - add only design-level boundaries.
- **Decisions**: Key technical choices with rationale (why X over Y?). Include alternatives considered for each decision.
- **Risks / Trade-offs**: Known limitations, things that could go wrong. Format: [Risk] → Mitigation
- **Migration Plan**: Steps to deploy, rollback strategy (if applicable)
- **Open Questions**: Unknowns that can safely be answered later without
  changing the specs, the approach, or the task breakdown. Omit if none.

Open questions are for genuinely deferrable unknowns, not decisions you
skipped. If a question would change the specs, the chosen approach, or
the task breakdown, resolve it now - ask the user instead of guessing.

Focus on architecture and approach, not line-by-line implementation.
The proposal covers why and what; design covers how. Reference the
proposal for motivation and, once written, the specs for requirements -
if a section would only restate them, point to them instead.

Good design docs explain the "why" behind technical decisions.
context:
This is the authorized greenfield Togarriapa/HermesAgent_Installer repository.
GPT-6.1 Sol owns specifications/task creation/refinement; GPT-6 Luna owns development.
Frozen baseline plans/2026-10-09-v1 plus immutable annotated tag must never change.
Append-only Sol amendments and live planning/OpenSpec artifacts evolve separately.
Target: Raspberry Pi5, nominal16GB RAM,1TB SSD, Coral USB or PCIe/M.2; detect actual facts.
Supported64-bit Linux ARM64, graphical user session for native official Hermes Desktop.
Thin shell bootstrap and typed modular Python; isolated dependencies, official Hermes PM Python3.14.
Upstream Hermes7085fbf7753266fc4943c55ac04926186bc90005; registry113f42d33be9e0c8f0f47f5ca998e687323dec83.
Read SOURCES.md and COMPATIBILITY.md for dated primary evidence; revalidate at configuration/update.
Preserve data/settings/credentials/private learning/unrelated services. No reimage/format/service takeover.
Runtime enforcement and Hermes-only correlated topology, no prompt-only authorization/sandbox claims.
Zero additional metered spending; privacy/budget/capability policy wraps all dispatch/background/retries.
One automatic long-term memory owner; preserve native session memory and provenance.
Native ARM64 Colibri GLM-5.2, experimental until measured; Coral separate delegate-used inference.
Official MCPs with harmless selected-resource reads and bounded init/discovery/reconnect/cancel.
User-facing installer/docs English, new schedules/display times Europe/Lisbon; preserve host timezone.
No physical target/accounts enrolled and no privileged installation on development Mac.
DoD: real adapters/handlers, meaningful fixture failures, source-to-spec/task/test/component/AC coverage,
strict OpenSpec validation, truthful distinct functional/account/hardware evidence and executable target workflow.
Cloudflare direct addition: blank hostname, secure scoped token, automatic owned tunnel/DNS/Access emailOTP setup.
Browser remote only official native Desktop app; loopback JWT gateway/WS expiry-revocation leases, no host desktop/shell/backend exposure.
Management token setup-only; active zone/owned conflicts/transaction resume, zero paid certificate purchase.
Preserve original12 acceptance criteria plus addedAC13..15; target/account mutation pending secure enrollment.
Planned commands/tests are not available/verified until implementation evidence exists.
